note: Schema 1 described a /dev/horizon0 ioctl transport (HZN_SCTL_*) and a /dev/native0 launch path. Neither device nor either ioctl exists anywhere in PowerEngine, so that wiring was a transport to an implementation nobody wrote. It was deleted rather than ported. What replaced it executes the guest's own ARMv7 instructions on the Cortex-A7 and reimplements Horizon around them, so the references that matter now are the ones that describe Horizon's kernel and IPC behaviour, not a syscall numbering.

used_for: SVC semantics, per handler, checked against every hzn_* implementation in source/horizon_kernel.c
HSYSCALL_DEFINEn parameter lists, which fix the AArch64 register order the 32-bit ABI is derived from
wait_process_wide_key_atomic argument order: x0 is the condition variable and x1 the mutex, the reverse of this kernel's parameter order (source/horizon_svc.c swaps them explicitly)
query_memory gap semantics: out of range reports INACCESSIBLE, a free gap runs to prev_vma->vm_end
get_system_tick and get_current_processor_number return a bare value, not a Result
build_result_response: HIPC reply layout and its deliberately over-reported raw word count (10 + payload words)
command_type enum and the IPC_ERR_REMOTE_PROCESS_DEAD close semantics
HSYSCALL_OUT writes the single out-value to regs->regs[1], i.e. x1 -- which is what makes r1 the out-register in the 32-bit derivation
the SVC number is the svc immediate (esr & ESR_ELx_xVC_IMM_MASK), matching minos_svc_frame.imm

struct horizon_hdr.is_64bit -- cited in include/horizon_image.h as the metadata a bare NRO/NSO does NOT carry, which is why horizon_image_probe_arch has to derive the architecture from the container itself
NRO0/NSO0 container layout and MOD0 placement, cross-checked against switchbrew

abi_derivations.note: No AArch32 Horizon SVC ABI exists in Reference/ -- horizon-linux's compat path is an explicit '// horizon TODO 32-bit syscalls'. The three decisions below are DERIVED from the AArch64 ABI, not transcribed. Each is stated with its reasoning and its falsifier at the top of include/horizon_svc.h.
abi_derivations.D1: arguments in r0..r7, results from r0, parallel to x0..x7 / x0..
abi_derivations.D2: 64-bit arguments occupy even-aligned register pairs, low word first (AAPCS). Observable at only three call sites -- svcWaitSynchronization, svcWaitProcessWideKeyAtomic, svcGetInfo -- each of which logs its raw r0..r7 frame on first call.
abi_derivations.D3: MemoryInfo is the ilp32 form with 32-bit addr/size; field order follows horizon-linux, which documents the two refcounts in the opposite order to libnx and wins as the in-tree source.

refused_by_name: AArch64 modules (a Cortex-A7 cannot execute them)
address aliasing: svcMapMemory, svcUnmapMemory, svcMapSharedMemory, svcUnmapSharedMemory (MVII is a flat 1:1 identity map)
services with no handler registered (hid, vi, nvdrv, fsp-srv and the rest)
SVCs this front-end does not implement

checked_in_disassembly: horizon_context_save / horizon_context_restore emit exactly the five written ARM instructions, no compiler prologue
guest entry brackets with cps #0x1f (System) / cps #0x13 (SVC) at both call sites
vwine_make_executable emits the full Cortex-A7 coherency sequence: DCCMVAU, ICIMVAU, BPIALL
